issues.legal_issue: A request to summon evidence may be refused when it is made after the evidence has closed to prove a factual basis that was known but was not pleaded in the suit.
material_facts: The suit challenged a registered adoption deed, which stated when the adoption ceremony occurred.
After the evidence had closed and the suit was listed for final arguments, the plaintiffs sought records concerning whether a defendant was on duty on the date of the ceremony.
The plaintiffs had not pleaded that the defendant's presence or duty status on that date undermined the adoption.
An application to amend the plaint to add the relevant allegation had been dismissed, and that dismissal had become final.
The suit was subject to directions for expeditious disposal.
issues.conclusion: The refusal to summon the records was proper, and the appeals challenging that refusal were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Evidence cannot assist a party in the absence of a pleading to support it. The court also relied on the fact that the relevant event was disclosed in the deed, the request came after evidence had closed, and expeditious disposal had been directed. The judgment identifies no statutory provision or earlier case as authority for this principle.

rule.if: civil_suit_evidence_request and evidence_closed and relevant_fact_known_at_filing and not supporting_pleading and request_is_late

predicates.civil_suit_evidence_request: A party in a civil suit asks the court to summon records as evidence.
predicates.evidence_closed: The evidence in the suit has closed before the party makes the request.
predicates.relevant_fact_known_at_filing: The party knew the factual basis for the proposed evidence when filing the suit.
predicates.supporting_pleading: The party pleaded the factual basis for the proposed evidence in the suit.
predicates.request_is_late: The party makes the request at a late stage of the suit.

issues.definition: When a party in a civil suit seeks records after evidence has closed to prove a fact known at filing but not pleaded, the request may be refused.

issues.legal_issue: A party may be refused a second request for the same evidentiary relief after an earlier request for that relief has been rejected.
material_facts: The plaintiffs first applied to summon records concerning the defendant's leave or service on the date of the adoption ceremony.
The trial court rejected that application.
The plaintiffs later filed another application seeking substantially the same records and relief in the same suit.
The trial court rejected the later application, and the Supreme Court upheld that rejection.
issues.conclusion: The rejection of the repeated application was proper.
issues.legal_principle: The court held that the trial court rightly rejected a later application seeking the very same relief after an earlier application had been dismissed. The judgment identifies no statutory provision or earlier case as authority for this conclusion.

predicates.civil_suit_evidence_request: A party in a civil suit asks the court for evidentiary relief.
predicates.prior_request_rejected: The court previously rejected the party's request for that relief.
predicates.later_request_seeks_same_relief: The party later makes another request seeking substantially the same relief.

issues.definition: When a party in a civil suit makes a later request for substantially the same evidentiary relief after an earlier request was rejected, the repeated request may be refused.
